statements.impact_statement: The bug is in the access-point side of 802.11w (hostapd code, built into wpa_supplicant only for AP/P2P-GO mode). beast-net's only wpa_supplicant configuration is generated by wpa_config() (beastnet/python/beastnet/wifi.py:182-221): one station network block with key_mgmt NONE, OWE, WPA-PSK and/or SAE, never mode=2 or P2P, so wpa_supplicant never acts as an access point.

Heap overflow in awk (editors/awk.c next_token). beast-net ships no link for awk (build/beastnet/userland.list 'exclude usr/*bin/...', which build/beastnet/mkinitrd.py:385 also applies to busybox applet links), so the code is in /usr/bin/busybox but never runs: /init, udhcpc.script, mdev.conf and the app only run the programs listed in beastnet/runtime.json 'binaries' and never call 'busybox <applet>', and busybox sh has no standalone-applet mode (with the shipped binary, a command without a link is 'not found').

PEAP is only used with key_mgmt=WPA-EAP and eap=PEAP. beast-net's only wpa_supplicant configuration is generated by wpa_config() (beastnet/python/beastnet/wifi.py:182-221): one station network block with key_mgmt NONE, OWE, WPA-PSK and/or SAE; it raises an error for 802.1X networks (wifi.py:220) and the UI does not offer them (wifi.py:46).

Terminal escape sequences in netstat output. beast-net ships no link for netstat (build/beastnet/userland.list 'exclude usr/*bin/...', which build/beastnet/mkinitrd.py:385 also applies to busybox applet links), so the code is in /usr/bin/busybox but never runs: /init, udhcpc.script, mdev.conf and the app only run the programs listed in beastnet/runtime.json 'binaries' and never call 'busybox <applet>', and busybox sh has no standalone-applet mode (with the shipped binary, a command without a link is 'not found').

Only b64decode() with an altchars argument is affected. statements.action_statement: ash ifsbreakup() heap overflow: busybox sh is /init and runs beastnet/rootfs/usr/share/beastnet/udhcpc.script, which word-splits DHCP-supplied values ($router, $dns), so a rogue DHCP server can feed it input. Wait for Ubuntu's fix (the shipped version is the newest in Ubuntu 26.04); when it is published, re-run build/beastnet/lock.py so packages.lock picks it up, then make build, make e2e and re-scan.

Per w1.fi advisory 2026-2, a malicious AP that knows a valid credential of one configured network can make wpa_supplicant accept an unrelated PMKSA entry. beast-net stops any running wpa_supplicant before each connection (beastnet/python/beastnet/net.py:313) and starts it with a single network block (wifi.py:182-221), and the PMKSA cache is in memory only, so every PMKSA entry belongs to the one network whose credential the attacker would already need; such an AP can complete the normal handshake anyway, so no authentication step can be bypassed.
